previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, COPD, insulin-dependent diabetes, and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for acute decompensated systolic heart failure and acute kidney injury, likely triggered by recent cocaine use and high-sodium food intake. He presented with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and ankle edema. Treatment included intravenous and oral diuretics to manage fluid overload, resulting in a 15-pound weight loss and improvement in symptoms. His kidney function improved with diuresis, and his insulin regimen was intensified due to poor glycemic control, with glargine increased to 50 units twice daily. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor daily weights, limit fluid and salt intake, avoid cocaine, and follow up with outpatient care.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to ___ for an exacerbation of your heart 
failure. This means your heart (which is a pump) was overwhelmed 
by the amount of fluid in your body. The reason for this is 
drinking too much water and eating too much salty foods. With 
too much water overloading the pump, this backs up into your 
lungs, causing shortness of breath. To avoid this, you should 
not take too much water (less than 2L), avoid salty foods, take 
your water pill (torsemide 200mg once per day), and weigh 
yourself every day; if your weight starts to go up more than 3 
lbs, call the heart failure clinic.  

We are arranging for a visiting nurse to help you with diet, 
medications, and weighing yourself. 

Please see your appointments and medications below.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Cardiology Team
